BRANCH TRAP, the easiest way to waste this task: lane infra lives on origin/develop -> release -> prod and does NOT exist on main nor on docs/youtrack-gap-analysis (the branch the plan session sat on, HEAD 4a9824f0). Branch from origin/develop; promotion is via .github/workflows/promote-billing.yml. DIAGNOSIS (proven, do not re-derive): billing.easybutt0n.ai/admin 502s on ~half of requests. NOT a missing hostname (it resolves and has ingress rule 2 on tunnel c5fdb916-947d-4440-95b9-88742bc4dcb0) and NOT a dead origin (mcp-billing-service up 15h healthy, sha-728a140, http://192.168.21.153:20251/api/health/ready = 200). Two causes combine: (1) /opt/mcp-cognizioware-uat/.env line 6 sets TUNNEL_TOKEN to a token decoding to the PROD tunnel, so billing-uat-lane-cloudflared-1 is a SECOND connector on prod - the token came from committed cloudflare/uat.env which is LABELLED uat but holds the PROD token, the exact mistake design/handoffs/billing-litellm-mcp-next-export.md:76 warns against; (2) ingress rule 2 points at http://mcp-billing-service:20251, a Docker DNS name, while every other rule uses a host IP - it resolves from cloudflared-uat (network mcp-cognizioware-networkk) but NOT from billing-uat-lane-cloudflared-1 (network billing-uat-lane_default), so whichever connector Cloudflare picks decides 200 vs 502. SCOPE SPLIT - STEPS 1 AND 2 ARE NOT THIS RUN'S: they are live prod changes outside git (a Cloudflare DASHBOARD edit repointing rule 2 to http://192.168.21.153:20251, and retiring the duplicate connector on CT100 with docker compose stop/rm -f plus blanking TUNNEL_TOKEN) - the gateway's Cloudflare MCP tools are READ-ONLY so the dashboard edit cannot be automated, and step 2 needs a pre-flight confirming no hostname is served ONLY by a lane connector (check b36c4501-88ac-481b-9005-10bc87c4d146). Overseer/Paxton do those; expect tunnel 16 -> 12 connections, still healthy. THIS RUN DOES STEPS 3 AND 4: remove the lane cloudflared service from deployments/tier/docker-compose.yml (~53-61), drop TUNNEL_TOKEN from env.dev.example and env.uat.example, correct deployments/tier/README.md, RELABEL EVERY COPY of the mislabelled prod token (cloudflare/uat.env, uat.env line 74, env.template line 76) since that file IS what caused the incident, point cloudflare/prod.config.yaml at http://192.168.21.153:20251, and update scripts/tests/validate_prod_tunnel_config.py so the guard FAILS on a container-name origin - a test that would not have caught this is not worth keeping. STEP 4 (separate bug, in scope): dev lane /api/health/ready returns 503 because ONE pending secondary ack sets degraded:true while secondary is 'disabled' and secondaryRequired:false - a disabled, not-required secondary must not make the service un-ready, and it matters because promote-billing polls /ready so the dev gate never goes green. HARD RULES: never run openclaw doctor (CLAUDE.md); never docker compose down -v on CT100; back up .env to a timestamped .env.bak- first; SKIP dotnet ef migrations add - HAND-WRITE migrations; the tunnel token is a CREDENTIAL - refer to it by tunnel ID or env var name, never paste it into repo/docs/commit; another agent has been iterating promote-billing so CHECK before touching it; no git add -A; do not push, do not merge. PR body must state plainly that steps 1 and 2 are operator actions and the repo change alone does not fix the live 502.
